why: This is a study-specific latent-profile application of Job Demands–Resources theory to AI-assisted language learning, not a general learning theory or a distinct theory of how people learn.

The Job Demands-Resources model is a general occupational well-being and work-motivation framework used here to organise conditions associated with teachers' professional-learning engagement, not a general theory of how people learn or are taught.

Job Demands–Resources theory is a general occupational wellbeing and work-motivation framework, not a learning theory, and the teacher-wellbeing model and cited predictor results do not warrant a canonical learning-theory page.

Job Demands-Resources theory is a general motivation-and-performance framework with an academic adaptation, but the closest canonical page, Self-Determination Theory (157), lacks its demands/resources structure and buffering or boosting interactions.

Job Demands-Resources theory is a general motivational framework linking contextual demands and resources, personal resources, motivation, engagement, and performance through main and moderation effects; the closest canonical page, Bioecological Model of Human Development (12), explains nested contextual influences on development but lacks the demands–resources motivational process and buffering or boosting mechanisms.

Job Demands-Resources theory is a general occupational motivation and performance framework, while the Academic Demands-Resources model is this study's adaptation rather than a general theory of how people learn or are taught.

The Job Demands–Resources Model is a general occupational stress and motivation framework applied to students, not a theory explaining how people learn or are taught, and the reported bright and dark pathways are empirical findings from one study.

The Job Demands-Resources model is a general occupational stress and burnout framework, not a general theory of how people learn or are taught, and the candidate does not independently constitute a learning-design page.

The Job Demands–Resources model is a general occupational stress and motivation framework, not a learning theory, and this proposal merely applies it to one study of university students' digital hoarding.
This is a study-specific application and extension of the occupational Job Demands-Resources model with grit, not a general theory of learning or teaching.
